items.label: Iran/Hormuz -- attacks surged to wartime highs the week of Oct 11-14; 6 vessels struck in a single day (Oct 11), the most since the war began; Brent ~$105
items.detail: Live web research (background-delegated, all figures sourced/dated): UKMTO confirmed 6 vessels struck in a single day on Oct 11, 2026 (5 tankers + 1 container ship) -- CNN (Oct 11) called it the highest number of incidents in a single day since the war started; CNBC (Oct 9) reported 11 tankers attacked in the week ending Oct 4; UKMTO logged 15 attacks Oct 6-14 (11 in the final 4 days); a tanker carrying 12 sailors was hit Oct 12; a strike off Qatar on Oct 7 was the first attack outside the Strait itself since Sept 9. Al Jazeera (Oct 14) reports attacks 'soaring' and oil flows crashing again; The National (Oct 13) confirms Iran is 'stepping up its campaign.' IMF PortWatch data (via an Oct 16 roundup) shows only 2 transits recorded Oct 11 vs. an 85/day pre-crisis baseline -- the strait is functionally choked, not merely disrupted. Brent ~$105.30/bbl intraday Oct 16 (down ~0.6% on the day, per HDFC Securities/Trading Economics), up from $100.20-100.32 on Oct 5/7 -- grinding higher through the escalation but not yet spiking to April 2026's $120+ levels. US crude inventories fell 8.6M bbl in the week ended Oct 9. DBC buffer ($43,423.20, 9.056% of NAV) held unchanged against this active, intensifying tail risk.
items.recommendation: No change to the DBC buffer recommended while the conflict is actively escalating rather than de-escalating -- re-evaluate buffer sizing only if Brent breaks meaningfully above the April 2026 ~$120 high, which would signal a step-change rather than the current grind. Have a human monitor UKMTO's daily feed directly given the pace of new incidents.

items.label: Fed/CPI/PPI all turned hotter -- odds of a 3rd 2026 hike at the Oct 27-28 FOMC jumped to ~51.5% (from 23.8% the day before the Oct 14 CPI print); hot PPI (Oct 15) pushed gold to a fresh high the same day
items.detail: Live web research (background-delegated): the Fed already hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% in Sept 2026 (first hike since 2023) -- this is a hiking cycle, not a cutting one. Sept CPI (released Oct 14): +3.7% y/y headline (vs 3.6% est, up from 3.4%), +2.6% y/y core (vs 2.5% est, up from 2.4%) -- both hot, driven largely by a 9.1% m/m gasoline spike (Hormuz pass-through). Sept PPI (released Oct 15) also came in hot per usagold.com's same-day report ('hot PPI fuels inflation-hedge bid'), though exact headline/core % wasn't independently corroborated beyond that framing. Market reaction: CME FedWatch probability of a further 25bp hike (to 4.00-4.25%) at the Oct 27-28 FOMC jumped to ~51.5% immediately after the Oct 14 CPI print, up from 23.8% the day before -- now roughly a coin-flip, not a settled case either way. FOMC Oct 27-28 confirmed on track per the Fed's own calendar (decision 2:00pm ET Oct 28, no SEP this meeting). This is a genuinely two-sided signal for TLT: duration risk is elevated by rising hike odds, while precious metals are rallying anyway on inflation-hedge/safe-haven demand rather than falling on higher real rates -- a stagflation-style dynamic, not a clean directional call.
items.recommendation: No trade action this run -- the decision is 12 days out. Re-run the TLT/precious-metals correlation and cohesion check the morning after the Oct 28 decision specifically, since a confirmed hike (now a real possibility, not a tail case) would pressure TLT duration while potentially extending the metals rally -- the two positions may move in opposite directions on the same news, which is itself worth re-measuring rather than assuming the current correlation structure holds.
